subject: RFI: prioritized model mix, throughput SLOs & burst allocator
messages:
From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@pioneerhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: prioritized model mix, throughput SLOs & burst allocator

Diego —

Thanks for taking this. Attached is Pioneer Health's RFI workbook (tabbed by model family and workload profile). We need a detailed answers pack on the following so procurement can finalize the reserved capacity section:

- Recommended GPU mix (typical steady-state + burst) for an initial deployment supporting 3 models: clinical summarization (long-context), conversational assistant (chat), embeddings (semantic search).
- Expected throughput (tokens/s or qps) per GPU type for our baseline input distributions and 95th latency SLO targets (50ms for embeddings, 250ms for chat, 800ms for summarization).
- Reservation/commitment strategy to meet peak month spikes (20% sustained burst for 6 hours/day) and how Redwood handles overflow to hosted capacity.
- Any constraints on quantized variants vs FP16 in terms of quality and throughput.

Please respond with a filled worksheet and short narrative. Procurement needs this by EOD Friday (14 Aug) to keep our timeline.

Attachment: pioneer_rfi_workbook.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks,
Tim
Tim Lee
Director, Cloud Procurement
Pioneer Health Systems
procurement@pioneerhealth.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Tim Lee <tim.lee@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: prioritized model mix, throughput SLOs & burst allocator

Tim —

Appreciate the workbook. We've completed the sizing worksheet and added a short runbook for the reservation + burst allocator behavior. See attached: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx. High-level answers up front, followed by the worksheet notes (we filled your tabs):

High-level recommendation:
- Steady-state: 6x A100-80GB for chat & long-context summarization split (4 A100 for chat/summary, 2 A100 for embeddings serving quantized T4-like capacity via mixed nodes).
- Burst pool: 2x H100-80GB hot pool for elastic heavy summarization runs (short-lived, high-throughput jobs).
- Cost-optimized baseline for embeddings: 6x T4-equivalent instances via shared nodes behind batching cache.

Throughput & SLO guidance (95th):
- Embeddings: T4-equivalent — 50 qps / node, 95th latency ~ 40ms (meets 50ms SLO with KV cache).
- Chat (short context): A100 — ~200 tokens/s per GPU under our optimized kernel path; 95th latency ~180–240ms depending on response length and batching.
- Summarization (long context 16k): H100 recommended for burst heavy sequences — A100 steady-state gives ~40–60 tokens/s; H100 burst gives 120–160 tokens/s. Expect 95th latency ~700ms steady / ~450ms on H100 during burst.

Reservation strategy:
- Commit to a baseline bundle (example: 6 A100 + 6 T4-eq capacity). Redwood Dedicated supports a reservable hot pool (2 H100 hot nodes) that you can reserve as optional burst units.
- Policy: baseline handles 80% of predicted peak; hot pool auto-attaches when queue depth > X or when rolling 5-min token rate exceeds baseline by 15%.
- Overflow: when both baseline and hot pool saturated, requests route to Redwood Hosted API (controlled fallback) with rate-limited throttling and fallback model that preserves core function. This is captured in the runbook tab.

Quantization & quality notes:
- 8-bit quant models give 2–3x throughput improvements for embeddings and chat with minimal quality regression for embeddings and classification prompts. For clinical summarization we advise FP16 or 4-bit tuned variants only after validation on your test prompts (we added a validation checklist).

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (spreadsheet with worksheet entries); sla-exception-form.pdf (if you need SLA tweaks).

Next steps:
1) We can run a 2-hour workload calibration session (SE-led) this week to validate throughput on a Pioneer sample prompt set.
2) If results align, we'll provide a formal reserved capacity quote and order form for signature.

Neha and Marissa — flagged for technical & commercial follow-up on calibration and order.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive — Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.com
From: Tim Lee <tim.lee@pioneerhealth.com>

Date: Wed, 13 Aug 2025 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: prioritized model mix, throughput SLOs & burst allocator

Diego —

Thanks for the fast turn. A couple quick clarifications before we route to infra: 

1) For the embedding capacity you recommend "T4-equivalent instances via shared nodes" — can you confirm whether those are dedicated T4 machines or multi-tenant nodes with strict isolation? We require data isolation for UK/EU patient data workloads (we may partition later).
2) For the auto-attaching hot pool: how do you bill the burst H100s while attached vs idle? We need clarity on billing during teardown windows (your procurement team prefers per-minute billing on hot pool).
3) On the quantization guidance: can you point to any back-to-back evals comparing 8-bit vs FP16 on clinical summarization? Even a short BLUF summary will help our model validation team.

If possible, please include a note on lead time for adding two H100 nodes to the hot pool in a Dedicated environment.

Thanks — aiming to send to infra by EOD tomorrow.

—Tim
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Tim Lee <tim.lee@pioneerhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 17:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: RFI: prioritized model mix, throughput SLOs & burst allocator

Tim —

Answers inline below, and a concise action list at the end.

1) Embedding capacity isolation:
- We offer both dedicated T4 nodes (single-tenant) and shared lower-cost nodes with namespace-level isolation. For regulated PHI workloads we recommend dedicated nodes (meets isolation and audit requirements). We note this in the worksheet (column: isolation_requirement).

2) Billing for hot pool H100s:
- Billing model options (we captured these in the runbook tab):
  a) Reserved hot-seat: monthly commitment for H100s with discounted hourly effective rate (recommended if you expect repeated daily bursts).
  b) On-demand attach: billed per-minute while attached; a 10-minute minimum tear-down billing applies to prevent thrash.
  c) Pre-warmed standby: small per-hour reservation to keep kernel warm + fast attach; charges lower than full attach but higher than idle.
- Per-minute billing for on-demand attach is available and we can specify tiered rates in the quote.

3) Quantization evals for clinical summarization:
- We ran a short head-to-head on a 200-sample Pioneer-like test set last quarter (internal eval id: SUM-CLIN-2025-Q2). Summary: 8-bit (GPT-style quant) reduced token inference latency by ~2.5x with an average ROUGE-L drop of ~0.8 points vs FP16 on out-of-sample clinical notes. For high-risk sections (medication, dosage), we observed occasional token-level hallucinations at 8-bit; recommended workflow: use FP16 for final pass or use 8-bit for first-pass draft + FP16 finalization. We included the short results snapshot in the spreadsheet appendix.

4) Lead time for adding 2x H100 to Dedicated environment:
- Typical lead time: 7–10 business days from signed order for us to provision and validate the nodes in your Dedicated cluster (can be expedited to 3–5 days for an upfront infrastructure fee). We documented provisioning steps and validation checklist in the runbook.

Action items / next steps:
- I'll schedule the 2-hour calibration with Neha (SE) — propose Fri 15 Aug 09:00–11:00 PDT (or Mon 18 Aug). Please confirm a slot and share the sample prompt set (S3 link or secure upload).
- Marissa will follow up with a reservation quote and a variant for on-demand hot-pool billing options.
- I'll prepare an abbreviated 2-page quantization memo for your model validation team (will attach to the HubSpot record).
- If procurement is comfortable, we'll move to draft order form; DocuSign link (placeholder) is in the related links.

Thanks — we'll be ready to get this validated before your infra deadline.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive — Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
